Use ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_: Use ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, for the IterLoop key. This is the standard pattern for third-party Anthropic-compatible gateways: it avoids the two variables colliding, since Claude Code otherwise prefers a set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to an empty string keeps it out of the way.

Answers to the most common questions abo: Answers to the most common questions about credit, top-ups, refunds, and usage-based pricing on IterLoop.
Yes. New accounts automatically receive: Yes. New accounts automatically receive a $2 credit as soon as you register, whether you sign up with email or with Google. There is no code to redeem, it is applied for you.
How do I add funds to my account?: How do I add funds to my account?
IterLoop is pay-as-you-go. You can top u: IterLoop is pay-as-you-go. You can top up any time with a card via Stripe, and charges are settled in Australian dollars (AUD). The preset top-up amounts shown adapt to your site language, or you can enter a custom amount, with a minimum charge of A$1.00 per top-up.
What happens if I get a refund or file a: What happens if I get a refund or file a dispute?
If a top-up is refunded or disputed thro: If a top-up is refunded or disputed through Stripe, IterLoop removes the matching share of credit from your balance in proportion to the refund. A full refund removes the full amount that was credited to you, and a partial refund removes only a proportional part. If a dispute is later resolved in your favor, the credit that was removed is restored to your balance.
No. Your credit balance does not expire: No. Your credit balance does not expire or reset over time. Note that this is separate from API keys, which can optionally be given their own expiry date when you create them.
Yes. Stripe automatically emails a payme: Yes. Stripe automatically emails a payment receipt to the email address you used at checkout.
When a request reuses a cached prompt pr: When a request reuses a cached prompt prefix, those cached input tokens are billed at a reduced rate below normal input pricing, shown as the "Cache" price on the pricing table. Writing a new entry to the cache costs a bit more than normal input, which reflects the one-time cost of creating that cache.
You are only billed for tokens that were: You are only billed for tokens that were actually generated. If a request fails before producing any output, it is fully refunded and costs you nothing. If a request streams some output before failing partway through, you are billed only for the tokens it actually produced.
